title: Don't allow enumeration of serial ports (or do it separately).
body:
As written on the [mailing list post](https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/mozilla.dev.webapi/wykkibp6BKo):

A: getPorts() would allow fingerprinting, IMO. The severity depends on when you want to allow access to the API (e. g. when `navigator.connectSerialPort()` [1], that reduces fingerprinting to users who opt in; whereas when prompting the user upon the first data received via serial port[2] and allowing to query all available ports, that allows straight fingerprinting.

B: Selecting the port to talk to should be up to the UA (mitigating A), listing the available ports (e. g. with a LRU list at the top) with the permission prompt […], i. e. a getPorts() method is not necessary. The API should allow a mechanism to connect to multiple devices […]

So, **tl;dr**, with additional thoughts not covered above: - `getPorts()`/`requestList()` allows fingerprinting, a no-no. - Once you grant access to the API, and you are not restricting access on a port-by-port basis, a script can go rogue (intentional or not, doesn't matter) enumerating and connecting to all devices it can find. Bad for the user, and restricting API adoption (browser vendors may not like that functionality). - The user should select the port to connect to (maybe using LRU and displaying some hardware information like manufacturer and pnpId where appropriate to aid the user in selecting the right port). - The problem is with non-UI environments like node – they need a port enumeration feature. Is this out-of-scope for the spec? If not, can this be made a separate API that is optional to implement or requires further privileges (e.g. via a separate prompt <-- bad UX, or chrome/elevated privileges).
